title: Intervalized headcount resilience & price-scan (Q2–Q4 2026)
content:
Quick summary:
This sheet ties a short Q2–Q4 2026 headcount plan to a small pricing-sensitivity sweep and an actionable trigger ladder. Objective: produce a compact, operationally actionable plan that preserves SLA budget and throughput under ±price shocks while protecting core product hires in Eng/Serving/ML.

Key assumptions (explicit):
- Time window: Mar 1 2026 (Q2 start) through Sep 30 2026 (end Q4 planning window).
- Baseline ARR run-rate used for sensitivity: $98.7M annualized (Feb 2026 trailing).
- Average fully-burdened FTE cost (finance estimate): Eng $27.5k/mo, ML $33k/mo, SRE $29k/mo, Product $18k/mo, GTM/Sales $16k/mo, Support/CS $12k/mo.
- GPU + infra baseline (hosted + dedicated amortized): $2.6M for the period (3 quarters pro-rated), variable proportion scales with token volume.
- Quantization / Optimize initiatives assumed to deliver 9% token-cost savings in Base, up to 14% in higher-adoption Surge.

Scenarios (intervalized):
- Base (prob. 55%): steady growth, pricing flat, token volume +12% vs plan.
- Surge (prob. 25%): demand spike, token volume +40%, revenue +18% (if pricing held).
- Downside (prob. 20%): price compression or macro decline, token volume -8%, revenue -22% (price-driven).

Headcount plan (summary, planned hires across window):
Role | FTE start Mar-1 | Planned hires (net) | FTE end Sep-30 | Avg comp/mo | 3q comp run-rate
Eng (platform + runtime) | 62 | +10 | 72 | $27,500 | $2,970,000
ML / Applied | 18 | +4 | 22 | $33,000 | $1,386,000
SRE / Infra | 14 | +3 | 17 | $29,000 | $522,000
Product / PM & UX | 10 | +2 | 12 | $18,000 | $162,000
GTM / Sales & AE | 22 | +6 | 28 | $16,000 | $432,000
Support / CS | 26 | +2 | 28 | $12,000 | $180,000
Total FTEs (start) 152 -> (end) 171; incremental 19 hires. Total 3-quarter payroll increment (net over baseline): $5.652M (includes ramp phasing; detailed sheet tab has month-level staffing curves).

Non-payroll variable cost sensitivity (notes):
- Token-inflated infra and GPU: roughly linear to token volume until saturation; model: baseline $2.6M * (1 + token_delta).
- Quantization adoption reduces token cost; we model net effect on infra = infra * (1 - quant_savings).

Pricing sensitivity sweep (illustrative):
Price change | Estimated revenue (3q) | Adj EBITDA impact (3q) | Hiring action signal
-20% | $18.9M (vs $24.6M baseline 3q) | -$4.1M margin gap | HARD FREEZE (stop all non-core hires + contractors)
-10% | $22.1M | -$1.8M margin gap | SOFT FREEZE (pause GTM non-essential hires, re-evaluate in 4 weeks)
0% (base) | $24.6M | baseline | proceed with planned hires
+10% | $27.1M | +$1.9M uplift | ACCELERATE key product/ML hires (use variable hiring uplift pool)
+20% | $29.5M | +$4.3M uplift | consider earlier Dedicated capacity purchases to secure pricing

Trigger ladder (operational rules, automated checks):
M1: Weekly rolling revenue burn vs plan (7-day smoothing). Thresholds: -10% -> alert finance + growth; -18% -> CFO + hiring freeze; -25% -> exec war-room
M2: Token-cost per 1M tokens (30-day MA) > baseline * 1.12 -> throttle new non-core customer onboarding and enable caching recommendations to customers.
M3: GPU spot price index (external feed) spikes > 35% over baseline 14-day -> pause burst pools and move non-latency jobs to preemptible queue.
M4: Headcount pipeline (offer + acceptance + start dates) snapshot: if acceptance rate < 70% for two consecutive weeks -> move 50% of planned hires to contingent contractors (3-month convertible contracts).

Operational playbook by trigger (short):
- Soft Freeze (-10% revenue): suspend GTM marketing spend, defer non-critical infra migrations, accelerate quantize & Optimize rollout to customers with cost-sharing discounts.
- Hard Freeze (-20% revenue): halt all new hiring except critical SRE/serving runtime safety roles (pre-approved list), convert 30% of open reqs to contractor sourcing, renegotiate 60-day vendor payment terms for cloud credits, pause non-billable pilot capacity.
- Surge (+15% rev growth sustained 6 weeks): accelerate hiring (convert contingent pool to FTE), pre-purchase committed Dedicated capacity (3–6 month), expand burst-credit quota and bill to committed bucket to preserve unit economics.

Micro-scenarios and margin math (concise):
- Downside example: a -20% price step decreases 3q revenue by ~$4.9M vs base; combined with +8% infra pressure (adverse token mix), net cash gap for the window ≈ $7.1M. Hiring and contractor conversions can recover ~$3.2M of that (payroll deferral + contractor flex), leaving a residual gap covered by reserve credit line or delaying Dedicated acquisitions.
- Surge example: +20% price with +40% token volume increases infra cost ~+40% but revenue uplifts more, net margin improves ~+$3.6M; recommended action: accelerate ML hires by up to +3 beyond plan, advance Dedicated purchase to lock capacity pricing.

Risk register (top 6):
1) Offer acceptance and ramp slippage (mitigate with signing bonuses + remote-friendly negotiating).
2) Token volume elasticity mis-estimated (mitigate via customer-facing pilot metering).
3) Cloud market spot volatility (mitigate via burst-credit policies and regional routing).
4) Quantize rollout slower than expected (plan B: incremental pricing add-ons for customers that opt in early).
5) Competitive price compression (run weekly competitor price tracker and propose promotional cadence).
6) Legal/compliance delays for Private deployments (hold a 3-person EC approval for necessary hires to avoid full freeze).

Open questions / to validate:
- Validate hiring ramp assumptions with Eng leads: average time-to-productivity (we used 12 weeks for eng, 8 weeks for GTM).
- Confirm contractor conversion budget/cost (legal + payroll overhead) with People Ops.
- Align expected uptake of Optimize quantization tooling per customer cohort; current adoption rate used: 18% base.

Next steps (action items):
- Diego: push month-by-month staffing ramp tab with hiring calendar (deadline: 2026-03-17).
- Priya: run a second sensitivity with a hybrid model-level price tiers (deadline: 2026-03-22).
- Finance: schedule weekly trigger digest to execs if any M1–M3 thresholds hit (start: 2026-03-15).

Appendix (short):
- Detailed month-by-month financials + per-role hire calendar are in the attached sheet tab ("month-runs"). This Drive doc is the summary anchor for exec review.
- Suggested comms template for a Soft Freeze (internal): one-paragraph CFO summary + 2 bullet actions for People Ops and Growth.

Notes to reviewers: keep comments inline; this is intentionally compact. If we want a more conservative approach, swap the 3q payroll ramp to a 50% front-load (delay remaining hires into Q1 2027).
